claims.claim_text_verbatim: To address this, we propose Multi-Agent Self-Supervision (MASS), an RSI method that alternates between evolutionary workflow optimization and supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.
claims.claim_summary: MASS alternates evolutionary workflow optimization with supervised fine-tuning on self-generated trajectories.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Through an evolutionary search constrained by structural guardrails, the model optimizes these computational-graph-like orchestrations, discovering the most effective distinct roles and information routing for a given task.
claims.claim_summary: Evolutionary search discovers effective roles and information routing for given tasks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Over two MASS cycles with Qwen3.6-27B, the model achieves 1.2–1.6× higher performance per output tokens on four open-ended public benchmarks.
claims.claim_summary: Qwen3.6-27B with MASS achieves 1.2-1.6x higher token efficiency on public benchmarks.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Because the improved model subsequently acts as a better optimizer and evaluator, this alternating framework enables a continuous, recursive bootstrapping of the model’s capabilities.
claims.claim_summary: MASS enables continuous recursive bootstrapping as the model becomes a better optimizer and evaluator.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Moreover, multi-agent traces are also more training-efficient: a student trained on them outperforms a single-agent student trained on 1.4× more training tokens.
claims.claim_summary: Multi-agent traces outperform single-agent training despite using 1.4x fewer tokens.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across two MASS cycles, the trained model’s win rate against the base model on the three test tasks increases from 53.9% to 69.9% (Section 4.2, Figure 3b), and on the four research benchmarks (MLR-Bench, ScienceAgentBench, DSBench, and AstaBench) its score per output token is 1.2–1.6× that of the base model (Figure 2).
claims.claim_summary: MASS increases test task win rate to 69.9% and benchmark token efficiency by 1.2-1.6x.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Notably, post-training only on task-solving trajectories improves all three roles in the RSI loop: task solving, workflow optimization, and evaluation (Section 4.2, Figure 3).
claims.claim_summary: Post-training on task-solving trajectories simultaneously improves solving, workflow optimization, and evaluation.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The trained model discovers high-quality workflows faster, and the evaluator accuracy increases from 73% to 93%.
claims.claim_summary: Evaluator accuracy rises from 73% to 93% while workflow discovery speeds up.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further find that optimized workflows develop more task-specific information handoffs and routing, consistent with our information-flow hypothesis (Section 4.3).
claims.claim_summary: Workflows evolve more task-specific information handoffs and routing during optimization.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The first-cycle multi-agent student achieves a 68.3% win rate against the base model, compared with 64.0% for a single-agent student trained on approximately 1.4× more processed supervised tokens (Section 4.4, Figure 6).
claims.claim_summary: First-cycle multi-agent student hits 68.3% win rate, beating single-agent training with 1.4x tokens.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our ablations further identify workflow optimization, rather than evaluation, as a major bottleneck in the homogeneous RSI loop (Section 5.1).
claims.claim_summary: Workflow optimization is identified as the primary bottleneck in homogeneous RSI loops.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Finally, trajectory analysis provides evidence that post-training internalizes information-handoff behaviors (Section 5.2).
claims.claim_summary: Post-training internalizes information-handoff coordination behaviors into model weights.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Performance improves on ScienceAgentBench from 28.7% to 31.8%, on MLR-Bench from 1.58 to 2.40, on AstaBench from 0.053 to 0.067, and on DSBench from 0.473 to 0.482.
claims.claim_summary: MASS improves performance across ScienceAgentBench, MLR-Bench, AstaBench, and DSBench.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On the three test tasks, L(1) achieves a 53.9% win rate against L(0), while L(2) reaches 69.9%.
claims.claim_summary: Win rate against base model rises from 53.9% in cycle 1 to 69.9% in cycle 2.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Directly comparing successive generations, L(2) also shows a larger gain over L(1), with a 60.8% win rate, compared with the 53.9% win rate of L(1) over L(0).
claims.claim_summary: Cycle 2 model achieves a 60.8% win rate over the cycle 1 model.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In this transfer setting, workflows optimized by L(1) outperform those optimized by L(0) in 64% of comparisons on average across 11 iterations and 12 tasks.
claims.claim_summary: Workflows optimized by L(1) beat those from L(0) in 64% of comparisons.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Optimized workflows increasingly place task-specific information in what agents communicate and how they are routed, while reducing redundant information across workflow components.
claims.claim_summary: Optimization increases task-specific routing information while reducing cross-component redundancy.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Jointly learning coordination from orchestrator trajectories and bounded execution from subagent trajectories may provide more effective RSI supervision than learning both from a single agent’s long-horizon trajectories.
claims.claim_summary: Joint learning of coordination and subagent execution provides superior RSI supervision.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Both M and M + exceed this piecewise-linear reference at their respective token budgets by 8.3 and 6.3 percentage points.
claims.claim_summary: Multi-agent models outperform single-agent token efficiency references by 8.3 and 6.3 points.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: More directly, M + reaches 68.3% with 28.82M processed supervised tokens, 4.3 points above S++ while using 31.4% fewer tokens.
claims.claim_summary: M+ reaches 68.3% win rate using 31.4% fewer tokens than S++.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Delegation rises from 1/110 trajectories for L(0) to 48/110 for L(1) and 87/110 for L(2), while code handoffs rise from 1/110 to 42/110 and 83/110, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: Delegation and code handoff occurrences increase dramatically across generations without prompting.
